items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-09-08
items.q: I never did like Georgia Boy's playing. You heard the talk of him. Oh yeah. I never did like his playing.

ctx.x: Well, I'll try to find one of those, too. But you were going to explain to me how a trumpet player would be playing certain long notes and the things he would do in jazz, the long notes, you know, he'd be playing a whole note.

Well, you mean, that's what I mean, playing a melody, you see, and to keep from affecting the melody, well, that's the only place that you could put your runs in, you see. You play your melody, like you said, da-da-da-da-da-dee-da. See? Right there is where you put your effects at, right in there, you see. Because when you say, no, you still, that's the melody, you see. You could go off and then you catch the melody and the next ball, you see. That's when a fella wanna play jazz. Jazz is nothing but a fill in,…
That's funny, I heard a lot of people don't like him. What was wrong with this playing?
